original_question: Let H : Top0 -> Set be an irreducible subset system, and let a T0 space X be called super H-sober when its Smyth power space PS(X) is H-sober. If {X_i | i in I} is a family of super H-sober spaces, must the product space product_i X_i also be super H-sober?
target_in_paper: Xu’s product problem for super H-sober spaces: let H: Top0 → Set be an R-subset system, not assumed to have property M, and let {X_i | i ∈ I} be a family of super H-sober spaces. Is the product space ∏_{i∈I} X_i super H-sober?
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient category Top0, the relevant datum H: Top0 → Set, the notion of super H-sobriety via the Smyth power space P_S(X), and the actual closure-under-products question for an arbitrary family {X_i}_{i∈I}. In substance, it is very close to the paper’s intended H-sober-space problem.
missing_details: The official formulation explicitly says that H may not have property M. This is the key hidden point, because Xu had already proved the product theorem under the extra hypothesis that H has property M; the open problem asks whether that hypothesis can be removed.
The paper’s standard term is 'R-subset system' (short for irreducible subset system).
It is best to say that {X_i}_{i∈I} is an arbitrary family of T0 spaces and that the product carries the usual product topology.

To reflect the paper’s actual intent, the question should make clear that it is about whether arbitrary products of super H-sober spaces remain super H-sober without any a priori property-M assumption on H.
refined_question: Let H: Top0 → Set be an R-subset system, with no a priori assumption that H has property M, and let {X_i}_{i∈I} be an arbitrary family of T0 spaces such that each X_i is super H-sober, i.e. the Smyth power space P_S(X_i) is H-sober. Must the product space ∏_{i∈I} X_i, equipped with the product topology, also be super H-sober?
justification: The draft is targeting the H-sober-space part of the paper, not Conjecture 1.1 on strong d-spaces. The exact nearby problem-faithful formulation is Xu’s 'Problem 1' about products of super H-sober spaces. The arXiv abstract states that the paper proves every R-subset system H automatically satisfies property M and gives positive answers to Xu’s questions. In the later journal version of the same H-sober discussion, Problem 1 is stated exactly with the crucial caveat 'may not have property M', Definition 5.4 gives the precise meaning of 'super H-sober', Proposition 5.3 proves that every R-subset system has property M, and the post-Proposition-5.3 summary says this yields positive answers to Problems 1–6. So your draft is essentially right, but it should explicitly include the absence of a property-M hypothesis, since that is what makes the question paper-faithful rather than merely repeating an already-settled special case.
